title: Compose every interlocking into a journey

facts.note: Plan artifacts are identifiable by path/kind. The rule is state-based: it applies to any plan whose current content declares one or more interlockings, whatever was or was not edited.
Validation runs at CONFIRM and its findings block CONFIRM; the harness must report the current phase.

Whether the plan declares interlockings must be read from the plan graph (validation subject_kind: interlocking); a plan-graph observer is needed. No particular edit or preexisting finding is required for activation.

fires: At CONFIRM, a plan declares interlockings but declares no journey (vacuous topology): every interlocking is reported.
At CONFIRM, a plan declares journeys, but an interlocking is neither a journey entrypoint nor the destination of any continuation reachable from one.
At CONFIRM, a plan whose only change is adding an interlocking, or a plan that was not edited at all but already leaves an interlocking outside every journey (non-exhaustive examples).
At CONFIRM, after a journey entrypoint is retargeted, a continuation endpoint is changed, or a continuation/journey is removed, so an interlocking is no longer reached (non-exhaustive examples).
doesNotFire: A plan that declares no interlockings at all.
Checking whether declared journeys' continuations are themselves closed (that is planner.journey.continuation-closure).

given: A plan that declares one or more interlockings (regardless of what was edited).
when: The plan is validated at CONFIRM, where any finding of this rule blocks CONFIRM (confirm-blocking).
then: Declare at least one journey and make every interlocking reached by a journey: as a journey's entrypoint interlocking or as the destination of a continuation reachable from that entrypoint.
prefer: For each interlocking, state the journey that starts it (what triggers the routing decision) or the continuation that leads into it from a reachable interlocking.
Decide the end-to-end flow: for each interlocking, state what happens after its train completes via continuations.
avoid: Stopping the decomposition at interlockings so it looks complete while the end-to-end flow was never decided.
A plan with interlockings and no journey (vacuous topology), relying on continuation-closure passing vacuously.
Orphan interlockings: routing decisions with no stated trigger and no stated place in the product flow.
why: The journey is where the plan says what starts a routing decision and what happens after its train completes. planner.journey.continuation-closure only validates the journeys a plan declares, so plans with none, or with interlockings outside every journey, would pass it vacuously.
evidence: Validator journeyCompositionFindings reports no findings at CONFIRM; enforcement is confirm-blocking, so any finding blocks CONFIRM.
Each finding carries interlocking_id, journey_count and reason, identifying the uncomposed interlocking and whether the plan has zero journeys.
verifier_detail: composed_interlocking: an interlocking that is the entrypoint of at least one journey, or the destination of a continuation reachable from a journey's entrypoint.
vacuous_topology: a plan with interlockings and no journey. Every interlocking is reported, because none of them is composed.
Validation: family=closure, template=graph_route_space_closure, variant=planner_journey_composition, phase=CONFIRM, enforcement=confirm-blocking, subject_kind=interlocking.

Context: planner.journey.continuation-closure validates only the journeys a plan declares, so it passes vacuously on plans with no journeys or with interlockings outside every journey; this rule covers that gap.
Enforcement: confirm-blocking — findings of this rule block CONFIRM.
audit: source name: Every interlocking is composed into a journey

sharedNodes.text: Disposition strict: the rule fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.
